filename: Recent increase in the observation-derived land evapotranspiration due to global warming._
title: Recent increase in the observation-derived land evapotranspiration due to global warming
testbed_rationale: The study produces an upscaled observation-driven global dataset of ET / sensible heat flux using offline ML models on weather station data; it is an offline statistical retrieval rather than an atmospheric/climate model parameterization testbed.
pain_points: Machine learning models show larger uncertainties in coastal areas (e.g., Australia) and areas with significant moisture/heat exchange due to oceanic influence and non-stationary conditions.
Data quality and sparse spatial distribution of weather stations limit model performance in certain regions.
Inability to fully capture atmospheric circulation and non-stationary surface/boundary-layer dynamics purely through empirical statistical methods.
extraction_notes: The paper uses ANN and RF to upscale flux tower latent heat flux (LE) and sensible heat flux (H) globally using weather station data from 1975-2017 based on boundary layer energy budget principles.
